versions.notes:
- Room for accessories fixed to the body: things held in either hand, horns or antlers, a necklace, something on the back, at the hip, on the wrists, ankles and belly, and a tail. A piece held or fixed this way keeps its shape as the avatar moves. The packs that fill these places come next.
- Wardrobe packs can now add hair styles too, which the Hair tab lists beside the maker's own.
- An avatar that wears something from a pack you've since uninstalled keeps it in its look. The maker says what isn't shown and which pack to install, and it comes back once the pack is installed again. A saved file still holds only what's worn.
- A lip colour you pick stays on the lips. It used to reach a little past them onto the skin round the mouth; now it fades in softly from the lips' edge, the way the made-up skins paint their lips.

- Hair moves: the long, ponytail, braid, bob and angled bob styles swing as the avatar moves, and settle back into place when it stands still. In a VRM, the 3D Avatars agent and other VRM apps swing them. The head, neck, shoulders, arms and back keep the hair out.
- A **Moving** pose in the maker's pose list turns the head now and then, so you can see the hair swing. A tail swings in the maker too.

- The face moves: avatars blink, shape their mouth as they talk, and look happy, angry, sad, relaxed or surprised. In a chat, the 3D Avatars agent plays these on both VRM and GLB files.
- Teeth and a tongue inside the mouth, seen when it opens.
- The eyes turn to look. In a VRM, the 3D Avatars agent and other VRM apps move them.
- A **Face** list under the picture plays it all in the maker: blinking and looking at you, talking, or one expression held.

- Save as VRM: the Save tab now saves a `.vrm` file as well as a `.glb`. Import it in 3D Avatars as a VRM model. It stands in a T-pose and works in other VRM apps too. A tail swings as the avatar moves.
- The VRM's terms: put your name as the author, and choose who may use the avatar, commercial use, sharing and changes, and credit. Your choices are kept for the next avatar you save. A VRM wearing credited pack clothes always asks for credit to their makers.
- **Open** reads a saved `.vrm` back for editing, as it does a `.glb`.

- Took out two skins, Mid-toned and Viking tattoos. Their material files say AGPL-3, which doesn't match the CC0 their catalogue gives. An avatar saved with one of them opens with the default skin instead.

- New places to wear things: glasses, a face mask, earrings, rings and socks. The new Accessories pack fills them, and adds gloves and two hats.
- Gloves hide rings, and socks hide the toenails, the way gloves and shoes already hide the nails.

- Wardrobe packs: install a 3D Avatar Maker wardrobe pack and its clothes appear in the Clothes tab, each with a line saying which pack it's from and who made it. The first two are Everyday Women's Clothes and Everyday Men's Clothes and Suits.
- A saved avatar names the makers of any credited pack clothes it wears.

- Real nails on every finger and toe: short, medium, long or none, and toenails on or off, in any colour. Gloves and shoes hide them.
- 23 more skins, among them freckled, ginger, bronzed, Eurasian, tattooed and made-up ones.
- 15 more eye pictures: amber, hazel, sapphire and other natural colours, cat's eyes, reptile and dragon eyes, and a trial anime eye.
- Four brow styles and two lash styles with fine, natural hairs.
- 29 more sliders for the cheeks, ears, nose, arms and hands, such as jowls, a bulbous nose and knobbly knuckles. A new avatar starts with truer ears, nose and hands.

- Nails are now a part of their own on every finger and toe, so a nail colour has a clean edge.
- 46 new face sliders in eight groups (eyes, brows, nose, mouth, jaw and chin, cheeks, ears, head), with ready-made shapes for each, such as hooded eyes, a Roman nose or an underbite.
- 15 new body sliders for the arms, legs, torso and hips, and her bust.
- Races are presets on the same body: choosing one sets race sliders you can mix and adjust, plus height and limbs. Horns, tusks, a tail and beards are accessories anyone can wear.
- A first Anime proportions style, and clean-edged lip colour.

- First version: a Home tab where you build a 3D avatar for a character or persona and save it as a GLB file for the 3D Avatars agent.
- Male and female bodies in eight races, with build, face and proportion sliders, three ages, skin and eye pictures or colours of your own, 14 hair styles, and 78 pieces of clothing and armour.
- Save the look as a small file, or open a saved avatar again to keep editing it.
- The face doesn't move yet, so in a chat the avatar nods while it talks.

- 50 new pieces for the slots 3D Avatar Maker 0.1.10 added. Jewellery: four bracelets and bangles, five anklets, four necklaces and a spiked collar, three pairs of earrings, ear and face piercings, and four for the belly. Six kinds of horns and antlers, seven pairs of wings and two tails. Things to hold or carry: a sword, a microphone, a tennis racket, a shopping bag, a shoulder bag, a sling purse and an electric guitar. Also a headset, a head mirror, a stethoscope and two tactical vests.
- Horns, wings, tails, held things, earrings and the solid bracelets and anklets are fixed to one bone, so they keep their shape as the avatar moves.
- The pack now needs 3D Avatar Maker 0.1.10 or later.

- The hats, hoods, veil, headband, top hat, pith helmet and brass circlet from the retired Historical and Fantasy and Modern Casual packs are here now, with the same names, so saved avatars still find them. Clothes went to the new 3D Avatar Maker: Clothes pack.
- 15 new pieces: a Santa hat, a chef's hat, a fishing hat, a patrol cap, a sun visor, a swim cap, a steel helmet, an aero cycling helmet, a riding helmet, safety glasses, swimming goggles, sports sunglasses, a respirator mask, a gas mask and lace-top stockings.
- 24 of the 45 pieces are CC BY now. A saved avatar credits the maker of every CC BY piece it wears.

- Took out the cat mask, the hero mask and the lightning earrings. Their model files say AGPL-3, which doesn't match the CC0 their catalogue gives, so they are left out like other such items. 19 pieces remain.

- First version: 22 accessories for 3D Avatar Maker's Clothes tab: six pairs of glasses, two eye masks, a medical mask, pearl and lightning earrings, two rings, three lengths of gloves, four kinds of socks and leg warmers, a cloche hat and a Christmas hat.
- Every piece is from the MakeHuman community and free to share (CC0). Needs 3D Avatar Maker 0.1.04 or later.

- First version: 178 pieces of clothing for 3D Avatar Maker's Clothes tab in one pack. It replaces four packs: Everyday Women's Clothes, Everyday Men's Clothes and Suits, Historical and Fantasy Clothes, and Modern Casual Clothes. Their 75 garments are here with the same names, so saved avatars still find them; their hats and other headwear moved to the Accessories pack.
- 103 new pieces: 28 dresses, a suit, a jumpsuit and three sporty one-pieces, 13 tops, 17 pairs of trousers and shorts including swimming trunks, 5 skirts, 27 pieces of underwear and swimwear, and 8 pairs of shoes.
- Every piece is from the MakeHuman community. Most are CC BY, and a saved avatar credits the maker of every CC BY piece it wears. Needs 3D Avatar Maker 0.1.03 or later.

- If you installed Marinara with its Android app, pictures paint and your personas, cards and connections load again. The Engine there refused Modern Life Sim's requests with "401: Android local authentication required". They now carry the app's local secret, as the `mari` command's do, and only to the Engine on the same device.

- If someone is throwing a party or going to one, they won't make plans with you for those hours, even if you said you can't come. When you invite someone out, you can see the hours they have a party.
- If someone starts dating you knowing you already have a partner, they're okay with it. This also fixes the lives you're already playing.
- On a phone, you can drag the phone button with your finger.
- When a new season starts, people keep last season's outfit until the new one is ready.
- Fixes in the optional Adult Module.

- NPCs is a rule now, life by life: people who aren't in your cast, like a club's staff and its regulars. It's off by default in a new life; a life that already had them keeps it on. Off, they step aside with their pictures, nothing deleted.
- Once you're dating, you can stay the night at theirs, or have them stay at yours.
- No more getting stuck at the end of someone's party, after a lunch break that already went by, with a money request in the middle of an outing, or after reloading during a honeymoon night.
- In the optional Adult Module, the club's dancers and regulars are options that need NPCs.

- Cooking and food: a kitchen at home, twelve recipes, a Cooking skill, and dinner on a date at your place.
- A home of your own: Hillcrest on the hill, buying or a mortgage, furniture for each home, and people noticing where you live.
- People drop by, and you throw parties at home, lived room by room; friends throw theirs, and birthdays are parties now.
- Friends and family can live with you, as many as your home has rooms for.
- Anyone in the cast can be your family, partner, ex or rival from day one.
- Scenes do what's said: favours where they're told, money asked in your own words, outings that follow the talk, a memory for everyone there.
- Clearer Special Actions, work from home, half the practice for skills, and always a way on when the model can't answer.
- Many fixes, and more in the optional Adult Module.

- Contacts no longer freezes: opening it doesn't load your whole life again, and each part of someone's sheet is drawn on its own, so one that can't be shown is just missing and the rest is there.
- If a whole screen can't be shown, it says so, with a button to go back to the map, instead of leaving the game stuck.

- You can use your own pictures for what people wear each season or at work, and for you in any of your outfits: pick one and frame it yourself. Yours stays until you ask for a drawn one again.
- You can rename someone in Settings, and updating from their card brings a new name from the card too.
- When a model puts quotes in the wrong place or leaves part of a line out, the game still reads its reply, so turns in scenes aren't lost.
- The names on the clothes store's rack are sharp again. The phone's shop opens on its own inside a store, and going back returns you to the store with your cart.
- A fix in the optional Adult Module.

- People look like themselves in their pictures: their name, and whether they're a woman or a man, now go with every picture of them, so a character from a series looks like the one you know.
- You can choose how big pictures of one person are drawn, in Settings, right below the size of the other pictures.
- This season's new clothes are for who you play. A character who got dresses they'd never wear gets the season's clothes picked again.
- In the shops, only the things for sale move when you scroll. Eating from your backpack shows up on top of it. The clothes store shows the store behind the clothes again.
- The game finds Marinara however you run it, even from another device or on a secure connection.

- Models that think before they answer, like GLM or DeepSeek, no longer get cut off halfway: every call leaves them room to think, and one that still runs out gets a second try with more room.
- Reasoning has a new option, none, for models that can answer without thinking first.
- Pictures no longer flicker or load again while others are being painted, in Settings and on every other screen.
- Text on the phone, in the Guide and in What's New is sharp again.

- It looks more like a game: a new title screen, a welcome, a first-day card, the GUIDE (a searchable how-it-works app on your phone), a relationship chart in Contacts, and a redone profile.
- Everyone gets their own personality, read from their card, instead of twelve fixed types.
- Relationships go all the way: dating, moving in, engagement and weddings (with more than one partner if all agree), jealousy, open relationships and breakups, each in a scene.
- The town talks: people notice what you do, NEWS every Monday, and friends have opinions.
- Outings are one long scene; plans go on a calendar; birthdays.
- You start without a job: find one in JOBS, interview, get promoted.
- Money: BILLS, debt and eviction; HOMES to move. Five districts, and a motorbike or a car.
- Pictures of key moments, outfits by season, and manual or automatic pictures per life.
- Modules: optional extras you switch on for each life.

- First release, staging only: a modern life sim in its own Home tab.
- A town on a clock with places, opening hours, day and night, and four seasons of thirty days.
- A job, rent, needs and skills; a home with furniture, cooking and a closet; shops, a mall and online orders.
- A cast from your character cards: their weeks, archetypes and gift tastes read by the model, three bonds each, tier events, relationship steps and memories.
- Scenes told by a visual-novel narrator; sleep, knocking on doors and things to do together.
- Alpha: a save from before a change it depends on warns when opened.
- The Low magic layer's name and summary, and the magic items' Spell level filter, are translated in all 11 language packs.

- A Low magic layer, turned on when a game is created: magic is rare and feared. No spell above 5th level is offered, and no spell scroll above 5th level is found or sold. Every magic item still exists, but no shop sells one (the magic dealer and the scribe are gone, and temples and alchemists sell only mundane goods), treasure drops one about a fifth as often, and a town's fence is the one shady way to buy one. The Game Master keeps creatures of magic out of random encounters, may still build a fight around one on purpose, and, when the player gives no reason, decides at game creation why magic is rare in this world. Magic items' spell scrolls carry a Spell level filter. It needs Capability API 1.813.

- The whole SRD 5.1 in Game Mode: build a character from any SRD race, class, background and subclass, up to 20th level, and fight on screen by the SRD's rules against its 323 monsters, with its 325 spells, 966 magic items and every piece of equipment. It ships with 11 translations as language packs beside the English ruleset, and the Engine downloads only the one it is set to. It needs Capability API 1.812, whose numbers it now follows, upstream having taken 1.391 (the 5e minors move up one, to 1.392-1.812). A monk taken as a second or third class is proficient with shortswords, as the SRD's Multiclassing Proficiencies say.

- The first full release of 5e (SRD 5.1): the whole SRD 5.1 played in Game Mode, from character creation through tactical combat, in 12 languages. Its data is 0.451.0's; the version games pin keeps counting (452), so every existing game and install updates to it.

- No challenge 3 caster throws a 3rd-level spell that hurts everyone around it: a veteran battle priest casts Bestow Curse instead of Spirit Guardians, and a veteran pyromancer Magic Missile instead of Fireball (two veteran priests still wiped a 4th-level party in a Moderate fight, Spirit Guardians dealing over half the damage). The plain Arrow of Slaying names its 14 kinds and says a goblin takes Humanoid, a wyvern Dragon.
- Capability API numbers follow the Engine's renumbering after it merged upstream staging, where 1.379-1.390 are upstream's, so the 5e minors move up past them. Nothing plays differently.

- The 35 made-up casters (pyromancer, cryomancer, necromancer, enchanter, support, battle and nature priests) are as dangerous as their challenge rating: each rank's Armor Class, spell attack and save DC sit within 1 of its tier (novice and adept AC 13, +4, DC 12; veteran AC 15, +5, DC 13; master AC 16, +7, DC 15; legendary AC 18, +10, DC 18). A veteran battle priest cast Guiding Bolt at +8 and wiped a 4th-level party in a Moderate fight. The plain Arrow of Slaying says it is the family's name and to give an arrow of one kind, such as Arrow of Undead Slaying.

- Magic ammunition hits more often as well as harder: an Arrow, Crossbow Bolt, Sling Bullet or Blowgun Needle (+1, +2 or +3) adds its bonus to the attack roll as well as the damage (Capability API 1.812). It declares 1.812.
- The Light weapon property reads "Light (weapon)" on its chip and item tag, so each language can tell it from the Light cantrip: in Spanish it read "Luz" (illumination) beside the weapons.

- True Polymorph and Shapechange offer creatures only: a flying carpet, a dancing sword, an arcane hand, an illusory double or an animated object is no longer a form, nor what True Polymorph makes of an object. The creatures catalog marks what a spell, item or ability makes with a "Made by" filter.
- Spanish: the scimitar reads "Cimitarra" again, in its own name and the 22 other strings that name it (it read "Cimitaciónra").
- Polymorph and Animal Shapes leave out the SRD's ten swarms too, as Wild Shape does: a swarm is many beasts, not "a beast".
- Wild Shape no longer offers the SRD's ten swarms: a swarm is many beasts, not "the shape of a beast". The creatures catalog marks them with a Swarm filter.

- Every language's store-card description fits the Engine's 2,000-character cap, so the official catalog lists the SRD again: the German and French ones ran over (2,008 and 2,001). The sentence on starting equipment in your inventory is dropped from the description in every language, English included; the equipment itself is still offered.

- Translations ship as language packs, one download per language beside the ruleset file, and the Engine fetches only the language it is set to (Capability API 1.811): the ruleset file drops from 34 MB to 7 MB. The catalog lists each pack with its translated name and description for the store card.
- Each translation's package description says once, at its end, how to choose the ruleset, as the English one does: the earlier line, carried over from a draft, is gone.
- One long rest in 24 hours: "A character can't benefit from more than one long rest in a 24-hour period" (Capability API 1.810), counted on the game's clock from the start of the last one.
- Sheet layout 10: a sheet made before 0.438.0 has its cantrips marked prepared, so the GM's sheet summary lists them. The summary also names the character's features, fighting styles among them, and a warlock's invocations and pact boon.
- 81 more strings are translated, the Features tab among them.

- A carried weapon is drawn when it is used: the items block names weapons as drawn on use (Capability API 1.808), so a ranger's spare Longbow, a barbarian's javelins or a rogue's dagger can be attacked with without first being equipped, other drawn weapons put away. Only a character with Ritual Casting (a bard, cleric, druid or wizard, or a warlock with the Book of Ancient Secrets) casts rituals: the spells list names those features as what a ritual needs (Capability API 1.809). It declares 1.809.

- Translations for 11 languages (Arabic, German, Spanish, French, Hindi, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian and Simplified Chinese) ship in the ruleset file: every name, label and rules text, plus the package name and description. The license attribution stays in English.

- Ritual spells can be cast as rituals, for no slot, outside a fight: the spells list names its Ritual column as the ritual mark (Capability API 1.807). Cantrips come onto the sheet prepared, since they are always ready, so the GM's sheet summary lists them. It declares 1.807.

- Attribution for release: the package's license names SRD 5.2.1 (the encounter budget table) beside SRD 5.1, with its CC BY 4.0 notice, and credits the Open5e srd-2014 data; it says the SRD material was adapted and reformatted, and that the package is not affiliated with or endorsed by Wizards of the Coast; the package description says it includes SRD 5.1 and 5.2.1 material under CC BY 4.0 and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Wizards of the Coast. The Engine's Capability API numbers from 1.385 up moved two places (upstream took 1.385 and 1.386), so every number the package names moved with them. It declares 1.806, so translations dropped in as locales/<language>.json ship with it.
- A long rest ends temporary hit points (Capability API 1.804): "they last until they're depleted or you finish a long rest".
- The anthro wolf's head is a size bigger, in proportion to its shoulders; Head size in the Look card still sets it either way.
- Clothes are lighter: each piece keeps about two thirds of its triangles, chosen so it looks the same in the game, which makes the package about 3 MB smaller and quicker to download.

- Clothes refitted (second batch): tops, dresses, robes, coats and the cloak now fit closer and are built over what's worn under them, so a shirt no longer shows through a vest and layered outfits stay clean as bodies change.
- Trousers, skirts, leggings, boots and shoes sit closer to the body; the hood follows the head, with no dent at the ears, and the scarf moves with the neck.
- The breastplate's hem is one clean rolled edge with the faulds lapping under it, and gauntlet fingers are curved plates.

- Looks designed from cards (Settings → People → Design looks from their cards, off to begin with; New world asks too): the AI designs the built-in body of each character and your persona from their card, choosing their body, race, build, face, skin, hair, eyes and clothes from the game's own options. With …and from their card's picture, the picture goes along to a connection that can see pictures. Your own Look card choices stay over it, and a card's 3D model still shows.
- Anyone's look can be changed: every character in Who lives here has Look, and talking to someone, Look at them has Change how they look.
- Anthro dragon: the dark cracks on the throat plates are gone (the throat's skin had folded over itself when the neck was deepened), and the plates run cleanly up to the jaw.

- Armour refitted: chainmail, scale mail and the gambeson follow the body instead of standing off it, the plate cuirass is shaped to the chest and waist (no more barrel), and bracers and greaves sit close. Their skirts' patterns no longer shear as they flare.
- Gloves and gauntlets follow the fingers: leather gloves bend with each finger, and gauntlets have a plate for each finger joint over a leather glove.

- Hands: the built-in bodies have fingers that move. Standing and walking, hands hang open in a relaxed curl instead of flat and spread, and they close round a weapon or a tool. The animation library's idle holds loose fists; the relaxed stance (Settings → Display → Standing and walking) opens them, and As recorded keeps them. A dwarf's big hands and a gnome's long fingers bend at their own knuckles. Gloves and gauntlets hide the fingers and stay stiff until they're remade.

- Clothes, the first batch refitted: leather armour and the brigandine are tailored to the body instead of hanging off it, the pauldrons, the leather armour's shoulder pads and the tassets are overlapping plates fixed in place, and the bikini's cords go all the way round with bows on the hips (they used to sink under the skin). Bikini armour and the barbarian harness sit on the body too.
- Faces and beards: elf and tiefling women lose the gaunt shelf under the eyes, halfling and gnome women have smooth human faces, the half-orc woman is a woman, and beards grow from the cheeks and chin and turn with the head.
- Anthro wolf: the head tapers into the muzzle from the front, without the puffy cheeks under the eyes. Anthro dragon: a much deeper neck, underwear that fits before any slider moves, and a neck that draws in under a collar.

- Standing and walking, relaxed: the animation library's own stance has the feet wide, the arms held out and the elbows bent, as if ready for a fight. People now let their arms hang by their sides and stand with their feet nearer together, a female body a little more so, with a narrower walk. Menu → Settings → Display → Standing and walking: By their body, Relaxed or Graceful for all, or As recorded. Running, working and fighting are unchanged.
- Hair fits every race: the skin no longer shows through the hairline and temples of an elf, a halfling or a gnome.

- Races for the built-in body: dwarf, halfling, gnome, elf, half-elf, half-orc and tiefling, each its own shape instead of a human made smaller (a dwarf broad and short-legged, a gnome with a big head and long fingers). The Look card has Race, Tusks, Horns, Tail and Facial hair (a moustache, a goatee and four beards); anyone may wear any. Clothes, underwear and long hair follow a race's build. Lore words (ww:looks:dwarf) and your build's race set it, and there's a ready-made preset for each.
- Anthro wolf: the tail sweeps back and away from the legs, the claws grow from the fingertips and toes, and the eyes follow the Eyes slider.

- Anthro bodies in the Look card: a wolf and a dragon, male and female, with their own sliders (muzzle, ears or horns, tail length and thickness), fur or scale colours (the dragon's in the ten draconic ancestries), wings shown or hidden, and presets. They wear the human clothes, apart from hats, hair and footwear for now. A dragonborn gets the dragon body unless another is chosen.
- Every Look slider now starts at the body's own shape, with left smaller and right bigger and both ends labelled. Your own character's untouched sliders start neutral.

- Hair, polished: long hair is fuller and layered, the fringe stays off the eye, the angled bob is lighter, curls read as curls, and the parted, buns, shaved and mohawk styles are remade to match the rest. Every style now follows the face, ear, neck and age sliders, and long hair no longer dips into the back when you strike or turn your head.

- Hair and clothes for the built-in body: 14 hair styles (MakeHuman's and our own), and 78 pieces, from swimwear, crop tops, skirts and shorts to robes, gowns, chain, scale and plate, plus MakeHuman's modern clothes. Each follows the body's sliders.
- The Look card's Clothes: ready-made outfits (peasant, townsperson, ranger, mage, knight, barbarian, beach, modern casual), one piece per slot, a dye or colour of your own per part, and the cloak's hood up or down. Townsfolk dress for their work.

- The package is less than half the size (86 MB to under 38 MB) with nothing lost: the kit's models are stored compressed and unpacked quickly in the browser, creatures are bundled by family, and the built-in bodies' shapes are stored more compactly. Kit files load several times faster on phones.

- With the Engine on HTTPS, the server part calls it by the name on its certificate, so its AI and save calls work there too (certificate checks stay on, and calls never leave this machine).
- The SRD's paralyzed and unconscious rules are played in full: they fail Strength and Dexterity saves, and a hit from within 1.5 m is a critical hit.
- Nothing is saved over a world another browser has saved since: it's loaded again from the Engine's copy, with a line saying why.

- Your party moves about a fight by how they fight (melee closes in, archers keep their distance, casters stay back), follows more loosely day to day (Settings → People → Your party: close, normal or loose), and wanders a little when you stand still.
- When you sit or lie down, companions take a seat nearby, sit on the ground, or ask to squeeze in beside you, up to four on a log, bench or bed. Tents and beds have Lie down as well as Sleep.
- Abilities of your own in the sheet: uses that come back by rest or day, dice, a save; used from the fight bar or /use. Companions can have them too.

- Fights: creatures flee less (only when badly hurt, and undead, oozes and constructs never), a fleeing one can be chased and struck until it gets away, and one that comes back rejoins a turn-based fight once, with no more repeated "joins the fight".
- Saving reaches the Engine while you play, worlds made on another device no longer vanish from Load world, and outfits chosen by hand are kept. Rules fixes: heavy armour ignores Dexterity, a critical hit doubles only the dice, Multiattack uses each attack's own numbers.
- Settings → Display → Creature detail distance: creatures further off are drawn with fewer triangles from the same model.

- The built-in body gets MakeHuman's CC0 skins: young, middle-aged and old, each Caucasian, African or Asian, with an Age choice that also ages the face and body (adults only). Or keep a skin colour of your own.
- Nine eye pictures besides the eye colour tint, and twelve eyebrow and four eyelash styles in the Look card. Townsfolk get varied ages, skins, brows and lashes, and lore words like "old" or "middle-aged" shape them.

- Settings → People → Default skins with underwear (on to begin with): anyone with no underwear chosen wears the usual; off, the base skin shows unless underwear is chosen in the Look card.
- More hair style names for the new bodies (bob, braid, curly, afro, shaved, mohawk), offered when the kit has them.

- The built-in bodies, polished: a smooth jawline, closed lips, eyes with depth and a wet line, relaxed hands, and fine skin detail (pores, creases) in the texture rather than the shape.
- Underwear as real garments with waistbands, hems and seams, in styles to choose top and bottom in the Look card: briefs, boxer-briefs and boxers for both; bikini, thong and boyshorts for the female body; a bra, a sports bra or a bralette; or none.
